Dead shells, liquidations and worthless equity are excluded automatically from the DCF's own verdict; state/never_interested.txt adds names by hand (one TICKER  reason per line). These rows never enter the ranking.

STALE: DCF or Analysis older than the staleness threshold · PRICE_DRIFT: live price far from the price the DCF was built on — stored upside unreliable · NO_PRICE: no usable price, live or stored · NO_IV: DCF has no probability-weighted intrinsic value · NO_DCF: tracked company without a DCF model yet · SANITY_FAIL: the DCF's own sanity check tripped — its implied multiples sit outside the ticker's 10-year history; hover the badge for the reasons · CCY: the intrinsic value is denominated in a different currency from the live quote — upside mixes currencies · LOSS: latest-FY net income below zero · NEG_ROIC: latest-FY ROIC (ROE for financials) below zero — the ROIC column's number · LOW_ROIC: latest-FY ROIC (ROE for financials) below 15%, the bar the ROIC column colours against — informational; the ROIC checkbox hides these rows (and NEG_ROIC rows), a missing figure never hides · NEG_FCF: the DCF's base-year owner FCF is negative, so the model values a recovery (non-financials only) · HIGH_DEBT: debt/equity above 2x at the latest FY (non-financials only; same bar as the deferred-queue screen) · KNIFE: upside above 200% with the price in the bottom 5% of its own 10-year range — the market has repriced it for something the model does not carry · EVAL_FAIL: the tier-1 scorecard has fails (see the Eval column) · CHINA: weighted IV marked down (default 30%, --china-markdown) for PRC realisation risk — CNY/RMB reporters and the names in state/china_exposure.txt; the rank uses the marked-down upside, Weighted IV and Upside stay raw · TOSS_UP: the gap between price and the (adj.) IV is under 0.25x the model's own bear-to-bull band (the Certainty column) — the price sits inside the DCF's uncertainty; informational, the Clear verdict checkbox hides these rows · THIN_HISTORY: fewer than 5 annual periods of results in the Metrics.csv — the scenarios, and so the Certainty score, rest on little evidence; informational, the Clear verdict checkbox hides these rows; an unknown history never flags · Eval: tier-1 scorecard pass rate (F fails / W warns), from state/scores/. · Upside @15%: the base case rebuilt at a 15% required return (each DCF's own required-return table) against the same price — a discount-rate stress, not the verdict; the rank never uses it. · Rough filter: the checkbox hides rows carrying any of EVAL_FAIL, HIGH_DEBT, KNIFE, LOSS, NEG_FCF, NEG_ROIC, SANITY_FAIL; the rank is untouched, so untick it to see them in place. · Hide China: the checkbox hides CHINA-badged rows (the PRC markdown names). · ROIC ≥ 15%: the checkbox hides LOW_ROIC and NEG_ROIC rows; a missing ROIC never hides. · Clear verdict: the checkbox hides TOSS_UP rows, whose Certainty is under 0.25 either way, and THIN_HISTORY rows, with fewer than 5 annual periods behind the model; a row with no score or an unknown history never hides. All four are on by default, none of them moves a row, and a search ignores them: typing finds a hidden name too. · Certainty: (adj. IV − price) / (bull IV − bear IV), the band scaled by the PRC markdown where one applies — how many bear-to-bull bands the price sits from the value; signed, blank where the scenarios are missing, inverted or in another currency from the weighted IV. · Adj. upside: Upside on the weighted IV after the PRC markdown (CHINA badge) — the number the rank uses; equal to Upside elsewhere. Upside @15% stays the DCF's own, unmarked.
